pairs_touching.what_says_this: group_evidence (G0483) states directly: b (Step 291) finds 'the corpus's operation family O, the state-transforming subset T..., and the observation set O_K... are THREE distinct objects, not the single {O,T} cut candidate Steps 288-289 (a is Step289) had collapsed them into.' b's own S2178 confirms: 'Confirms, using the corrected three-way-separated model, that removing O, T and O_K together does not restore acyclicity - reinforcing that they are not substitutes for the equiv cut and refuting any residual reading of Step 288's "bootstrap boundary is O/T" claim even under the corrected object model.' b directly refines a's two-object (O,T) dependency-graph cut methodology into a three-object (O,T,O_K) model and re-confirms a's own headline finding ({equiv} as the unique minimal cut) still holds under the refined model.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If b's three-way object separation was developed independently of a's specific graph-cut methodology (e.g. purely from re-reading 259.7's five-kind classification, with the cut re-test being incidental rather than the point), the relationship would be closer to an independent correction of a shared upstream claim (Step 288) than a direct refinement of a itself.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 29 and 13 are NOT two graphs. One graph; a restricted CANDIDATE SET for cuts.
rationale_evidence.statement: Clarifies that the previously-reported '29 nodes' and '13 resolvable nodes' figures do not describe two different graphs but a single 29-node graph (used for cycle detection) together with a 13-node decision-resolvable subset (used only to restrict the candidate search space for minimal cuts); cuts found in the 13-node search are then tested for acyclicity against the full 29-node graph.
